PERMISSIONS AND WHAT THEY ARE FOR

• Notifications — the persistent notification of the background service. Android will not let the service run without one

• Accessibility "Return to sleep" — optional. Puts the device back to sleep right after drawing; without it the frontlight flashes on every lock. Nothing on screen is read and no events are intercepted, the service exists for a single system call

• Exact alarms — redraw the clock on schedule

• Internet — weather, news, book cover

• Wake lock, autostart, vibration — wake the panel to draw, start after a reboot, confirm an unlock

HOW IT WORKS

• The service listens for the screen turning off and draws the dashboard over the lock screen

• The panel is woken and put straight back to sleep, so the device reaches real sleep

• E-ink keeps the image at zero power

• The clock is redrawn at the interval you set; data refreshes in the background at its own

• Unlock with the fingerprint sensor — instant, with a short vibration

WHAT IS TAKEN FROM THE BIGME FIRMWARE

• Panel refresh mode. The app reaches into the firmware e-ink framework (xrz.framework.manager) and asks for one full clearing pass instead of flashing black then white — faster and cheaper on battery

• Waking without the frontlight. The wake lock carries the same name the firmware recognises from its own stock screensaver, so the panel wakes without lighting up

• Lifting the restriction on those calls. Android hides internal system methods from ordinary apps; the HiddenApiBypass library (an open-source LSPosed project) lifts that for the two names needed. Neither root nor an installed LSPosed is required

• All of it is optional: on any other device these calls are simply not found and the app works the ordinary way

FOR ANDROID 13 AND NEWER

Accessibility is blocked for apps installed outside an app store. Open App info, then the menu, then "Allow restricted settings" — after that the service can be switched on.
